Omar (sec-eng): Heads up — keystore rotation for eu-keystore (v3 -> v4) scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC. This will create new key versions and retire the old primary. Concern: DSAR erasure workers reference key-versioned ciphertexts. Need plan so deletions succeed and we keep provable audit records without exposing raw keys.
Kevin (eng-infra): +1. We can avoid downtime by granting a scoped, ephemeral role that can decrypt only for the TTL of the rotation job. Proposal: `dsar-erasure-runner` SA with limited KMS:Get* and storage:Delete on the deletion-bucket prefix. I'll outline RBAC bits below.
Jessica (platform-sre): We also need immutable deletion receipts (signed) kept in audit-log storage so Legal can verify later. Audit logs must include key id/version used for the op, actor, and deletion-hash.
Legal (legal): For DSARs we require a verifiable receipt: record id, sha256(record), timestamp, operator id (or service account), and KMS key-id used. A signed blob (JWS) attached to the DSAR case is ideal.
Kevin (eng-infra): Draft RBAC/KMS snippet — this is the minimal approach, will use short-lived creds from our token broker:
```
# create SA and rolebinding (example)
kubectl create sa dsar-erasure-runner -n erasure
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: dsar-erasure-runner
rules:
- apiGroups: ["redwood.io"]
  resources: ["deletionrequests"]
  verbs: ["get","list","patch"]
EOF
# KMS policy: allow Decrypt only for ciphertexts with tag dsar=true
```
Omar (sec-eng): Important: don't grant `kms:Decrypt` broadly. Use condition on request.resource.tag:dsar=true and bind to the ephemeral SA. Also ensure we capture the KMS key_id/version in the audit entry before the blob is removed.
Jessica (platform-sre): For logs, route the signed receipt and KMS metadata to the immutable audit index (write-once S3 prefix with object lock) + separate append-only index in our audit service. That covers tamper-proofing and search.
Omar (sec-eng): Another edge: rotation may leave orphaned encrypted snapshots referencing the old key version. We should run a pre-rotation scan for pending deletion jobs that reference old key-versions. Quick SQL to find suspects:
```
SELECT id, status, key_version FROM deletion_requests
WHERE status IN ('queued','in_progress')
AND created_at < now() - interval '2 hours';
```
Kevin (eng-infra): I'll run that query in staging now and run a dry-run delete against a canary partition. Plan: dry-run 08:30 UTC tomorrow, live run 09:30, rotation at 10:00. Dry-run will emit receipts to audit-dev.
Legal (legal): Confirming: receipts from dry-run are fine for QA, but we need final signed receipts for actual erasures. Also we may need retention-exception metadata if legal holds exist — include hold-id in the audit blob.
auditbot: Rotation job scheduled by deploy-bot for eu-keystore at 10:00 UTC (created_by: deploy-bot, run_id: rot-2026-08-12).
oncall (ops): I'll be oncall during the window. If any deletion job fails (status -> error), please @oncall immediately and include the deletion_request id. Also capture stderr from worker.
Omar (sec-eng): Action items: (1) Kevin: create ephemeral SA + KMS conditioned role and post IAM policy (2) Kevin/Jessica: run dry-run and post receipts link (3) Jessica: ensure immutable audit prefix and object-lock config (4) Legal: confirm receipt schema (5) Omar: run orphaned-snapshot SQL and escalate any hits.
Kevin (eng-infra): Will do. I'll post the IAM policy and a short checklist here once done. Will also include a fallback: if keystore rotation fails, we'll pause rotation and fallback to old key for 1 hour.
Jessica (platform-sre): Noted. I'll update the DSAR runbook with the rotation window and the fallback steps + contact list: @Legal, @Omar, @Kevin, @oncall.
Legal (legal): Thanks — please include an example signed receipt format in the thread when available.
Omar (sec-eng): Thanks all. Please react :thumbsup: to acknowledge.
Kevin (eng-infra): 👍 (will post updates around 07:30 UTC tomorrow).
